exercise.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Lateral Raise
library_steps: Hold a dumbbell in one hand and grip a post with the other.
Raise the dumbbell out to the side up to shoulder height.
Lower it slowly. Finish all reps, then switch arms.
exercise.one_line_summary: Standing tall, free hand holding an upright post; the working arm (left in the picture) rises out to the side, a little in front of the body, to shoulder height (90 deg) with a soft, fixed elbow and palm down. No shrug, no lean, no swing.

setup.target: Feet about hip-width, knees soft, trunk upright (no lean toward or away from the post).
setup.why: A still trunk stops momentum doing the lift.

setup.target: Right hand grips an upright post at about chest-shoulder height, arm out to the side and a little forward, elbow soft.
setup.why: Library steps; the post steadies the body so only the working shoulder moves.

setup.target: Neutral grip at the start (palm facing the thigh), turning to palm-down as the arm rises.
setup.tolerance: handle within 20 deg of level at the top
setup.why: ACE: closed neutral grip, wrists neutral.

setup.target: Down and back, held there the whole set.
setup.why: ACE cue; stops the upper trap taking over.

movement.measure: elev: upper arm from the side of the trunk, 0 = hanging, 90 = level with the floor
plane: 0 = straight out to the side, +90 = straight forward
handle tilt at the top (front end up = slight outward turn)
movement.end: front edge tipped up a little (tilt 18)

muscles.emg: 30.3 % MVIC, highest delt head (seated lateral raise, 60 % 1RM, S1)
muscles.role: Lifts the arm out to the side; what the exercise is for.
muscles.surface: Outer cap of the shoulder, from the acromion down to the outer upper arm.

muscles.role: Helps abduct the arm in the scapular plane.
Helps, more so because the arm rises a little in front of the body.

Library secondary; holds and turns the shoulder blade upward. Not lit: no EMG in the sources opened, and the cue is to keep it quiet (no shrug). Lit as secondary in the two-arm lateral_raise file, which has its own sources.
muscles.surface: Top of the shoulder between neck and acromion.

muscles.role: Starts the raise; lies under the trapezius.
muscles.surface: Under the trapezius above the shoulder blade spine.

muscles.role: Holds the dumbbell and the post.

mistakes.mistake: Raising above shoulder height or shrugging
mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Hand above the shoulder, shoulder hitched to the ear.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Upper trap takes over; impingement risk.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Trunk tilts sideways as the arm rises.

sources.citation: Campos YAC, Vianna JM, Guimaraes MP, et al. 2020. Different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals. J Hum Kinet 75:5-14.
sources.what_it_gave: Lateral raise, 60 % 1RM, 13 trained men: side 30.3, rear 24.0, front 21.2 % MVIC.

sources.citation: American Council on Exercise. Exercise Library: Lateral Raise.
sources.what_it_gave: Neutral grip start, elbows slightly bent and leading, raise to shoulder height, small upward tilt of the front edge past 60-70 deg, shoulder blades down and back, wrists neutral, no back arch.

clip_check.check: Right hand closed on the post, both pictures
clip_check.target: fist centre within 2 cm of the post centre line

clip_check.check: Left hand wraps the dumbbell handle
Side delt is the strongest red in both pictures
